entries.title: Selected geodesic costs can be dependent
entries.statement: INDEPENDENTLY CHECKED FINITE COUNTEREXAMPLE (w362-R001). On a square with four independent edge weights uniform on {1,2}, select the cheaper path between opposite corners, breaking ties toward the upper path. Conditional on upper selection, its two costs have covariance -5/121: the probability both equal 2 is 1/11, but the product of marginal probabilities is 16/121. The unconditional two selected costs have covariance -9/256. Their sum has variance 23/64; dropping covariance terms gives 55/128. Disjoint raw inputs therefore do not ensure independent costs after path selection. This is a finite obstruction, not a claim about planar fluctuation exponents.
assumptions: Finite square graph with two two-edge terminal paths

entries.title: Retention factor and persistent threshold covariance
entries.statement: AUTHOR-DERIVED FINITE IDENTITY, explicit referee acceptance pending. On a finite connected graph with iid Uniform[1,2] edge weights and fixed terminals, define clipped off-edge thresholds a_e in [0,1] so that centered coordinate costs are min(U,a_e)-a_e+a_e^2/2 for U uniform on [0,1]. For a<=b, K(a,b)=a^2[b(2-b)/4-a/6], and K is symmetric. Under independent rate-one coordinate refresh, Var(T)=integral_0^infinity exp(-t)H(t)dt, where H(t)=sum_e E K(a_e(eta),a_e(eta^t)) and only off-edge coordinates are coupled inside H. Its limit is the first-order Hoeffding energy L, not generally zero. H(t)-L is the sum over |S|>=2 of |S|exp(-(|S|-1)t)||T_S||_2^2. A full-kernel integrable decay envelope for all t is impossible when L>0. No lattice exponent estimate is asserted.
assumptions: Finite connected graph and distinct fixed terminals
Independent Uniform[1,2] coordinates and independent refresh flags
T_S denotes the orthogonal Hoeffding projection on coordinate set S

entries.title: Unproved crossover input for planar FPP
entries.statement: UNPROVED SUFFICIENT INPUT, not a theorem about FPP. For iid Uniform[1,2] undirected nearest-neighbour Z^2 passage times from 0 to n e1, restrict to the exact finite box [-2n,2n]^2. Let H_n and L_n be the threshold kernel and its first-order floor from the finite-product identity. A sufficient route to variance of order n^(2/3) would prove, uniformly in integer n>=1: L_n<=C n^(2/3); H_n(t)-L_n<=C n F(n^(1/3)t) for all t>=0 with nonnegative integrable F; and H_n(t)>=c n for 0<=t<=c' n^(-1/3), for positive constants independent of n. Upper and lower integral bounds then follow by substitution and persistence. All quantitative inputs remain unproved. A qualitative chaos statement, a kernel value only at t=0, or an assumed variance-growth ratio does not supply them. Current full-target openness is UNKNOWN as of this draft.
assumptions: Exact finite-box reduction for positive bounded edge weights
Quantitative inputs are a proposed proof obligation, not established hypotheses of the actual model

relations.rationale: The sufficient crossover bounds require the correctly normalized variance integral and separation of its persistent first-order floor.
The finite selection counterexample prevents substituting independent selected segments for the derived joint refresh coupling in the threshold identity.
